$comment: Ground truth for the invoice vision corpus. See README.md in this directory.
Ground truth is established by a HUMAN READING THE INVOICE — never by recording what
the model returned, which would enshrine today's errors as the standard.
Partial truth is fine: expectTotal alone still catches a model that drops line items.
THIS REPO IS PUBLIC. Synthetic and sample invoices only — see README.md.
$conventions: TAX IS NOT A LINE ITEM. app/actions.ts instructs the model to skip tax lines, so
expectLineItems and expectLineItemCount EXCLUDE tax, while expectTotal is the grand
total shown on the document, which INCLUDES tax. sum(expectLineItems) + tax = expectTotal.
SUMMARY LINES ARE NOT LINE ITEMS. Where a document restates a section subtotal (fixture
04 repeats an unitemised 'Labor $1,250.00' on page 2), the correct extraction keeps the
itemised rows and drops the restatement. Extracting both is double counting.
kind is this file's vocabulary: part | labour | fee | discount. The app's own field is
`category` with values parts | labor | misc, and it has no discount value — a negative
line is expected back as category 'parts' or 'misc' with a negative total_cost.
expectRejected is the pass condition for the non-automotive control: parseInvoiceLineItems
should return error NOT_AUTOMOTIVE_INVOICE rather than an extraction.
$provenance: All eight fixtures were generated synthetically on 2026-07-30 — no document here came
from a real shop, a real customer, or the internet. Shop names, addresses, phone numbers
and invoice numbers are invented. The phone numbers are not dialable — 555 followed by
eight digits is not a valid US number. The addresses use the state abbreviation 'ST',
which does not exist, so no address resolves anywhere; note that two of the five-digit
codes used (00733, 00735) do fall inside Puerto Rico's real range, which is why the
fictional state abbreviation, not the number, is what makes them unambiguously invented.
VINs use the DEMO* prefix from supabase/migrations/*seed_demo_vehicles.sql and are 21
characters, so they are not valid 17-character VINs.
JPEG fixtures carry no EXIF; PDF fixtures carry no author/creator/producer and a fixed
timestamp. Manufacturer part numbers are product identifiers, not personal data.
Vehicles deliberately match the three seeded demo vehicles (2018 Honda Accord Sport 2.0T,
2020 Subaru WRX, 2019 BMW M3 Competition) so uploads exercise extraction rather than
tripping the VEHICLE_MISMATCH guard. There is currently no fixture that tests that guard.

schema.case: what this fixture is testing — the awkwardness it represents
schema.isAutomotive: boolean. false = a control that validateConsultantDocument must REJECT
schema.expectRejected: boolean. true = a correct run returns NOT_AUTOMOTIVE_INVOICE, not items
schema.expectVendor: shop name as printed, or null if not asserting
schema.expectTotal: number, or null. The single most useful assertion
schema.expectLineItemCount: integer, or null. Catches silent truncation
schema.notes: anything a human needs to know — unreadable fields, ambiguity, why truth is partial

fixtures.case: Clean digital scan, itemised. The baseline — if this fails, something is badly wrong
fixtures.notes: Vector PDF, every field crisp. Invoice #NG-24831. Vehicle 2018 Honda Accord Sport 2.0T, VIN DEMO1HGCV1F30JA000001, odometer 93,140. Subtotal 209.65 + tax 17.30 = 226.95; the 17.30 must NOT appear as a line item. Two rows pair a labour charge with its part under near-identical names (Cabin Air Filter Replacement - Labor / Cabin Air Filter) — a model that collapses them will return 6 items.

fixtures.case: Phone photo at an angle with slight blur — how a real user actually captures one

expectLineItems.description: Hawk HPS Front Brake Pads HB533F.668

fixtures.notes: Invoice #CPG-1188. Vehicle 2020 Subaru WRX, VIN DEMO2JF1VA1G60L9000002, odometer 40,655. The real difficulty is geometric, not optical: perspective makes each row's baseline slope, so a description on the left sits visibly higher than its own qty/unit/amount on the right, and each description reads as if it belongs to the row above. Row-to-amount association is what this fixture tests. Every character remains legible to a human at full size. Subtotal 742.40 + tax 61.25 = 803.65.

fixtures.case: Faded thermal receipt — common at independent shops, low contrast
fixtures.notes: Ticket T-70455, timestamped 06/19/2026 10:42 AM. Vehicle printed as '2018 HONDA ACCORD' only — no trim and no VIN, so a correct run leaves VIN null and must not flag a mismatch on partial info. Print is faded overall with vertical bands where the head is worn; whole words sit inside those bands and are the likeliest misreads. All five amounts are legible to a human. 'NEXT SVC 99,812 MI' is a service reminder, not a line item. The card line reads VISA ************1000 — a fabricated masked number, no real PAN. Subtotal 153.45 + tax 12.66 = 166.11.

fixtures.case: Multi-page invoice — does it read past page one, or silently stop
fixtures.notes: Invoice #BW-2261, two pages. Vehicle 2019 BMW M3 Competition, VIN DEMO3WBS8M9C55J5000003. This fixture carries two distinct traps. (1) Truncation: page 1 holds only the four labour rows, so a model that stops after page 1 returns 4 items and a total near 1,250.00 — the shape of that failure is unmistakable. (2) Double counting: page 2's SUMMARY block restates 'Labor (see page 1 for itemization) $1,250.00'. That restatement must NOT be extracted; a model that takes it returns 12 items summing to 3,436.80 before tax against a printed subtotal of 2,186.80. Part numbers are printed in their own column (11517635803, 11537848577, 83192211191, 95770, 11427854445, 15A2D1) and belong in part_number, not in the description. Subtotal 2,186.80 + tax 180.41 = 2,367.21.

fixtures.case: Handwritten additions on a printed form — very common in small garages
fixtures.notes: R.O. 4472, date written as '7/6/26' — a correct run resolves that to 2026-07-06, and reading it as 6 July vs some other order is itself worth checking. Four line items, the R.O. number, the date, the vehicle, the odometer and all three totals are handwritten; only SHOP SUPPLIES 6.00 is printed, which makes a partial read easy to spot (printed row present, handwritten rows missing). Vehicle written as '2020 Subaru WRX', no VIN. The form has ten ruled rows and six are blank — blank rows must not become empty line items. Ignore the signature 'D. Reyes' and the margin note 'paid cash - thanks!'. HONEST LIMITATION: the handwriting is a chancery script face with per-glyph jitter, not a real hand. It is more regular than genuine handwriting, so this fixture almost certainly UNDERSTATES how hard real handwriting is. Treat a pass here as necessary, not sufficient. Subtotal 193.50 + tax 15.96 = 209.46.

fixtures.case: Parts and labour split into separate sections — tests structure, not just OCR
fixtures.notes: Titled REPAIR ORDER rather than INVOICE — worth confirming that alone does not cause a rejection. Invoice #MAW-3390. Vehicle 2020 Subaru WRX, VIN DEMO2JF1VA1G60L9000002. Three sections each carry their own subtotal row (Labor Subtotal 1,690.00, Parts Subtotal 1,160.75, Misc Subtotal 67.00); none of those three is a line item, and taking them yields 12 items and roughly double the subtotal. 'Rear Main Seal' appears twice by design — once as labour at 90.00 and once as a part at 18.40 — so a model that de-duplicates on description alone drops a real row and returns 8. Part numbers 15803HD, FW-SB6, 806732050, K0375Y0700 are in their own column. Subtotal 2,917.75 + tax 240.71 = 3,158.46.

fixtures.case: Line items with discounts and credits — negative numbers are quietly mishandled
fixtures.notes: Invoice #NG-25107. Vehicle 2018 Honda Accord Sport 2.0T, VIN DEMO1HGCV1F30JA000001, odometer 95,602. Three negative rows, printed with a leading minus (-$35.00, -$51.00, -$20.00). The failure to watch for is sign loss: returning them as +35.00 / +51.00 / +20.00 keeps the item count at 8 and still yields well-formed JSON, but the subtotal becomes 772.60 against a printed 560.60. A second failure mode is dropping them entirely, giving 5 items. Rotor Core Credit is qty 2.0 at -17.50 each; the line total is -35.00. Discounts are applied before tax, so tax 46.25 is 8.25% of the discounted 560.60, not of the gross. The app has no 'discount' category — expect these back as parts or misc with a negative total_cost.

fixtures.case: Non-automotive invoice (control) — validateConsultantDocument must REJECT this
fixtures.notes: THE PASS CONDITION IS REJECTION, NOT EXTRACTION. parseInvoiceLineItems should return is_valid_invoice false and error NOT_AUTOMOTIVE_INVOICE; validateConsultantDocument should likewise decline it. An accepted restaurant bill is a real bug and means the corpus has caught a validator that says yes to everything. expectVendor, expectDate and expectTotal are recorded because they are facts about the document and are useful for diagnosing a wrongful accept — they are NOT a target to extract. Check 0472, table 12, 07/18/2026 7:58 PM. Six food and drink items totalling 125.00, plus sales tax 10.31 and gratuity 25.00 = 160.31. Nothing on it is automotive; there is no vehicle, no VIN, no parts and no labour. Note that it does contain the words CHECK, SUBTOTAL, SALES TAX and TOTAL, which is precisely why a keyword-shaped validator would wave it through.
